collection.description: A teen's first day helping the builders is not going well: ask for one simple job, or keep trying everything.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Today (subject) gets to help the builders for the first time. (subject.He/She) has been looking forward to it for months. So far (subject.he/she) has dropped a bundle of thatch, tripped over a pole, and handed (friend) the wrong cord three times. (subject.He/She) is starting to wonder whether this was a terrible mistake.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "Could you give me one thing to do," says (subject), "and I'll do it properly?" (friend) hands (subject.him/her) the job of tying off the corners. (subject) does all four, slowly and very carefully. They're good. (friend) checks each one and nods. "Tomorrow you can do the walls," (friend.he/she) says. (subject) walks home feeling about three feet taller.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) keeps trying to help with everything at once. By the end of the day (subject.he/she) is covered in bits of thatch and has done a little bit of everything, mostly not very well. "Was I any use?" (subject.he/she) asks. (friend) thinks honestly. "Some. More than this morning." (subject) decides to take that.
